themeData.name: Ancient Table
themeData.description: Roman garum, Greek olive cakes, Egyptian flatbread - these recipes connect us to the dinner tables of Rome, Athens, and the ancient world.
themeData.coverImagePrompt: Ancient Roman or Greek dining room with amphoras and olive branches, classical architecture, archaeological illustration style

recipes.title: Apicius' Conditum Paradoxum
recipes.description: Melt honey in wine with pepper, bay leaves, saffron and dates. When warmed, pour into vessels for aging. The older it gets, the better it becomes.
recipes.story: This spiced wine from Apicius' 'De Re Coquinaria' (circa 4th century CE) was served at Roman banquets. The recipe showcases the Roman love of complex flavors and expensive spices. 'Paradoxum' means 'special' or 'paradoxical,' likely referring to its unique combination of sweet honey, aromatic spices, and pungent pepper. It was considered both a digestive aid and a symbol of wealth.
instructions: Combine honey wine with pepper, bay leaves, and saffron in a pot.
Heat gently, but do not boil.
Age for at least one month before serving.

recipes.title: Roman Patina de Piris
recipes.description: Patina de piris: pira elixa et purgata e medio teres cum pipere, cumino, melle, passo, liquamine et oleo modico. Ovis missis, in cumana facies, piper supra aspargis et inferes.
recipes.source: Apicius, De Re Coquinaria, Book IV
recipes.story: Patina (the origin of our word 'pan') was a Roman custard-style dish, both savory and sweet. This pear patina from Apicius demonstrates Roman sophistication in combining fruits, spices, and dairy. The use of passum (raisin wine) and exotic spices like cumin shows the extensive trade networks of the Roman Empire. It was likely served as part of the secunda mensa (second course) at elaborate dinners.
instructions: Poach the pears in honey and passum until tender.
Grind pepper, cumin, and lovage together.
Arrange pears in an oiled dish.
Bake in a moderate oven until set.
Serve warm with the poaching liquid drizzled over.

recipes.title: Greek Olive & Honey Cakes
recipes.description: Mix flour, honey, oil, wine. Shape, bake. Ancient Greek dessert.
recipes.story: Greek sacrificial cakes offered to gods, sweetened with honey—liquid gold of ancient world.

recipes.title: Roman Garum Sauce
recipes.description: The Roman ketchup. Mix fermented fish sauce with wine and honey.
recipes.story: Garum was Rome's most important condiment, made from fermented fish. Every kitchen had it.

recipes.title: Egyptian Flatbread
recipes.description: The bread of pharaohs. Simple flatbread cooked on hot stones.
recipes.story: Ancient Egypt's staple food, made from emmer wheat. Found in tombs as offerings.
instructions: Mix flour, salt, water into dough.
Cook on hot stone or griddle 2 minutes per side.

recipes.title: Mesopotamian Beer Bread
recipes.description: Bread made with beer, the drink of gods. Sumerian staple.
recipes.story: Mesopotamians invented beer and used it in baking. This bread sustained ancient civilizations.
instructions: Mix flour with beer, water, honey, salt.

recipes.title: Greek Lentil Soup
recipes.description: Philosopher's soup. Lentils with vinegar, the food Herodotus praised.
recipes.story: Mentioned by Herodotus. Spartans and philosophers ate this simple, nourishing soup.
instructions: Sauté onion and garlic in oil.

recipes.title: Roman Moretum
recipes.description: Peasant cheese spread. Virgil wrote a poem about making this.
recipes.source: Virgil's Moretum poem, Roman agriculture texts
recipes.story: Roman farmers' breakfast, immortalized in Virgil's poem 'Moretum.' Garlic cheese spread.

recipes.title: Persian Rice Pilaf
recipes.description: The royal rice. Saffron-scented pilaf with nuts and fruit.
recipes.source: Persian culinary traditions, Silk Road records
recipes.story: Ancient Persia perfected rice cooking. This pilaf graced royal tables of the Achaemenid Empire.
instructions: Sauté onion in butter until golden.

recipes.title: Byzantine Honey Fritters
recipes.description: Sweet fritters soaked in honey. Constantinople street food.
recipes.story: Byzantine Empire's popular dessert, served at festivals and sold by street vendors.
instructions: Make batter with flour, eggs, milk.

recipes.title: Greek Barley Cakes
recipes.description: Barley cakes with cheese. Olympic athlete fuel.
recipes.story: Ancient Olympic athletes ate these for energy. Barley was Greece's primary grain.

recipes.title: Roman Stuffed Dormice
recipes.description: A delicacy for wealthy Romans. Dormice stuffed and roasted.
recipes.story: Apicius' most exotic recipe. Dormice were fattened in clay jars and served at banquets.

recipes.title: Phoenician Fish Stew
recipes.description: Mediterranean fish stew. Phoenician sailors' food.
recipes.story: Phoenicia's maritime culture created this stew, spreading it across Mediterranean colonies.

recipes.title: Carthaginian Couscous
recipes.description: Ancient North African grain dish with meat and vegetables.
recipes.story: Carthage perfected couscous preparation. This dish predates Roman conquest of North Africa.

recipes.title: Etruscan Polenta
recipes.description: Porridge of the Etruscans. Predecessor to modern polenta.
recipes.story: Etruscans ate grain porridge (puls) before Rome adopted it. Foundation of Italian cuisine.

recipes.title: Sumerian Date Cake
recipes.description: Sweet cake studded with dates. Mesopotamian celebration food.
recipes.story: Dates were Mesopotamia's primary sweetener. This cake appeared at religious festivals.

recipes.title: Chinese Jiaozi Dumplings
recipes.description: Ancient Chinese dumplings. Medicinal food turned celebration dish.
recipes.story: Legend says they were invented by physician Zhang Zhongjing in Han Dynasty to prevent frostbite.

recipes.title: Viking Smoked Fish
recipes.description: Preserved fish, Norse survival food.
recipes.story: Vikings smoked fish for long voyages. This preservation method sustained Norse expansion.

recipes.title: Celtic Oat Porridge
recipes.description: Ancient Celtic breakfast. Oats cooked in water or milk.
recipes.story: Celts cultivated oats in Iron Age Britain. This porridge sustained warriors and farmers.
instructions: Boil water, add oats and salt.

recipes.title: Aztec Chocolate Drink
recipes.description: Bitter chocolate drink of emperors. Xocolātl.
recipes.story: Aztecs considered chocolate the food of gods. Drunk at ceremonies, served cold and bitter with chili.

recipes.title: Inca Quinoa Soup
recipes.description: Andean superfood soup. The mother grain.
recipes.story: Incas called quinoa 'the mother of all grains.' This soup sustained high-altitude civilizations.

recipes.title: Medieval Pottage
recipes.description: Peasant stew of grains and vegetables. Medieval Europe's daily food.
recipes.story: Pottage fed medieval Europe. A one-pot meal simmered all day, eaten with bread.

recipes.title: Roman Puls
recipes.description: Rome's original daily bread. Porridge before bread dominated.
recipes.story: Before Romans perfected bread, they ate puls—a grain porridge. Foundation of Roman diet.

recipes.title: Greek Symposium Wine
recipes.description: Diluted, sweetened wine for philosophical discussions.
recipes.story: Greeks never drank wine undiluted—considered barbaric. Symposiums featured this spiced, watered wine.
instructions: Mix wine with equal parts water.

recipes.title: Babylonian Beer
recipes.description: The world's oldest recorded recipe. Hymn to Ninkasi, beer goddess.
recipes.story: Babylonians brewed beer 4000 years ago. The Hymn to Ninkasi is humanity's oldest recipe, a beer-making song.
